findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the full wiring protocol for `provider_provenance` threading: enumerate each of the five `finalize_verdict` call sites, state whether each receives an assembled provenance record or emits `None`, and document the `None`-fallback semantics (e.g. recovery/degraded paths always emit `None`; only the happy-path coach step carries a real record) so AC4's test can be written to cover the boundary cases, not just the happy path.
evidence: AC4: 'a test asserts the 343b gap-5 wiring lands: the plan-review gate verdict carries `provider_provenance`, exercised through the real assembly path rather than a hand-built dict'
orchestrator.finalize_verdict signature (orchestrator.py:528-536): `(ctx, parts, *, coaching, coverage, runner_name, model)` — no provenance parameter

Ticket 343b gap-5 comment: 'thread provenance into finalize_verdict — either accept a provider_provenance argument from the callers that DO hold cfg (workflow_ops / gate_dispatch / drift_refresh), or pass cfg itself'
Three recovery call sites in gate_dispatch.py (lines 377, 441, 478) each call finalize_verdict with only cfg.runner and cfg.model — cfg IS in scope, but no assembled provenance record is present
workflow_ops.py:223 and :759 also call finalize_verdict — the latter inside the coach step which does not receive cfg directly

findings.finding: AC4 mandates that the 343b gap-5 wiring test exercises the real assembly path through `finalize_verdict`, but the plan never specifies the fix protocol: which of the five `finalize_verdict` call sites carry a provenance record, what signature change is made to `finalize_verdict`, and crucially what the None-fallback behavior is for the three recovery/degraded call sites (`_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`, `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`, `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`) that today receive only `cfg.runner`/`cfg.model` and hold no assembled provenance record. Without this protocol, an implementer may thread provenance through the happy path only and leave the recovery paths silent — exactly the bug gap-5 documented — or may add a defaulted `provider_provenance=None` to `finalize_verdict` with no AC verifying recovery-path behavior.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, item 4 (the 343b gap-5 wiring test)
scenarios: Implementer threads provenance only through the happy-path `plan_review_coach` step (workflow_ops.py:759) and leaves the three gate_dispatch.py recovery paths emitting None — the test passes (happy-path exercises finalize_verdict), but a verify-failure or coach-failure recovery still ships a missing provenance field

Implementer adds `provider_provenance=None` default to finalize_verdict and wires only the workflow_ops happy path, satisfying AC4's test while leaving drift_refresh and the degraded path without provenance — the same gap shape as before the story
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the AC or the Approach section with: 'Add `provider_provenance: dict | None = None` to `finalize_verdict`. The three gate_dispatch.py call sites (`_recover_plan_review_coach_failure`, `_recover_plan_review_verify_failure`, `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`) pass `None` — they hold `cfg.runner`/`cfg.model` but no assembled provenance record. The workflow_ops.py happy-path call site passes the record from its StepContext inputs (threaded from the runner via the workflow output). AC4's test must assert both that the happy-path verdict carries a non-None `provider_provenance` AND that a recovery-path verdict carries `None` (or explicitly documents that recovery paths are out of scope for this story).'
